title: A2 Writing Quiz 2 — Weekend Plans & Changing Weather

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Have you ever broken your arm?
Have you ever break your arm?
Did you ever broken your arm?
Have you ever broke your arm?
questions.explanation: Present perfect question: Have + subject + past participle: 'Have you ever broken your arm?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I have joined the gym two months ago.
I joined the gym two months ago.
I have join the gym two months ago.
I am joining the gym two months ago.
questions.explanation: A finished time expression ('two months ago') requires past simple, not present perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I was watching TV when the storm started.
I watched TV when the storm was starting.
I was watch TV when the storm started.
I watching TV was when the storm started.
questions.explanation: Past continuous (background) + past simple (interruption): 'I was watching TV when the storm started.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This summer is hoter than last summer.
This summer is more hot than last summer.
This summer is hotter than last summer.
This summer is hottest than last summer.
questions.explanation: One-syllable adjective, double final consonant + -er: 'hotter than'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: That was the best holiday I've ever had.
That was the goodest holiday I've ever had.
That was the most best holiday I've ever had.
That was the better holiday I've ever had.
questions.explanation: Irregular superlative of 'good' is 'the best': 'the best holiday'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I couldn't sleeping because of the noise.
I couldn't sleep because of the noise.
I not could sleep because of the noise.
I couldn't to sleep because of the noise.
questions.explanation: 'Couldn't' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'couldn't sleep'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: You don't have to take medicine, it's just a cold.
You haven't to take medicine, it's just a cold.
You don't has to take medicine, it's just a cold.
You not have to take medicine, it's just a cold.
questions.explanation: 'Don't have to' means it's not necessary: 'You don't have to take medicine.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: You should have worn a coat, it was freezing.
You should wore a coat, it was freezing.
You should have wear a coat, it was freezing.
You should has worn a coat, it was freezing.
questions.explanation: 'Should have' + past participle expresses regret about the past: 'should have worn'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We're going to visit the doctor tomorrow.
We're going visit the doctor tomorrow.
We going to visit the doctor tomorrow.
We're go to visit the doctor tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' + base verb expresses a plan: 'We're going to visit the doctor.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If you don't rest, you will feel worse.
If you won't rest, you will feel worse.
If you don't rest, you feel worse.
If you rest, you will felt worse.
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb: 'If you don't rest, you will feel worse.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She avoids eating fast food.
She avoids to eat fast food.
She avoids eat fast food.
She avoids ate fast food.
questions.explanation: 'Avoid' is followed by a gerund (-ing form): 'avoids eating'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I decided going to the doctor.
I decided to go to the doctor.
I decided go to the doctor.
I decided for going to the doctor.
questions.explanation: 'Decide' is followed by the infinitive with 'to': 'decided to go'.

questions.question: There aren't ___ clouds in the sky today.
options: much
many
a little
much of
questions.explanation: 'Clouds' is countable and plural, so 'many' is used in negative sentences.

questions.question: I only have ___ minutes before my swimming class starts.
options: a little
a few
much
little
questions.explanation: 'Minutes' is countable, and 'a few' means 'a small number of'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'however'.
options: It was cold. However, we still enjoyed the walk.
It was cold, however we still enjoyed the walk.
However it was cold we still enjoyed the walk.
It was cold however, we still enjoyed the walk.
questions.explanation: 'However' starts a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'It was cold. However, we still enjoyed the walk.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I go jogging every morning in order to stay fit.
I go jogging every morning in order stay fit.
I go jogging every morning for to stay fit.
I go jogging every morning in order to staying fit.
questions.explanation: 'In order to' + base verb expresses purpose: 'in order to stay fit.'

questions.question: The medicine should arrive ___ Friday.
options: until
by
since
for
questions.explanation: 'By' means 'no later than' a certain time: 'arrive by Friday.'

questions.question: It rained a lot ___ our trip to the mountains.
options: during
while
for
since
questions.explanation: 'During' is followed by a noun phrase describing a period of time: 'during our trip.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "I am tired.")
options: He said that he is tired.
He said that he was tired.
He said that he tired.
He said he be tired.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'am' shifts to 'was': 'he said that he was tired.'

questions.question: Which is the correct way to start an email to a close friend inviting them for a walk?
options: Dear Sir/Madam,
Hi Aygun,
To Whom It May Concern,
Dear Customer,
questions.explanation: 'Hi [Name],' is the natural, friendly greeting for a close friend.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to end a casual email to a friend?
options: Yours faithfully,
Best wishes,
Sincerely,
Yours sincerely,
questions.explanation: 'Best wishes,' is a warm, semi-informal closing suitable for friends.

questions.question: Choose the correct suggestion.
options: How about going swimming this weekend?
How about go swimming this weekend?
How about to go swimming this weekend?
How about we going swimming this weekend?
questions.explanation: 'How about' + gerund is used to make a suggestion: 'How about going...'

questions.question: Which sentence correctly combines 'This is the doctor.' and 'The doctor treated my father.'?
options: This is the doctor which treated my father.
This is the doctor who treated my father.
This is the doctor what treated my father.
This is the doctor treated my father who.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is used for people in relative clauses: 'the doctor who treated my father.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She rarely feels dizzy in the morning.
She feels rarely dizzy in the morning.
Rarely she feels dizzy in the morning always.
She feels dizzy rarely in the morning.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency usually go before the main verb: 'She rarely feels dizzy.'

questions.question: Which sentence has correct punctuation?
options: Do you know why the gym is closed today?
Do you know why is the gym closed today?
Do you know why the gym is closed today.
Do you know, why the gym is closed today?
questions.explanation: Indirect questions keep normal word order and end with a question mark: 'why the gym is closed today?'

questions.question: It ___ since this morning, so the streets are flooded.
options: rains
has rained
has been raining
rained
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous emphasizes an ongoing action with duration: 'has been raining'.

questions.question: These running shoes aren't ours, they're ___.
options: they
them
theirs
their's
questions.explanation: Possessive pronoun (stands alone, no noun after it): 'they're theirs.'

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses sequencing words.
options: First, check the weather. Then, pack an umbrella. Finally, leave early.
First check weather then pack umbrella finally leave early.
Finally check the weather, first pack, then leave early.
Then first check weather, finally pack leave early umbrella.
questions.explanation: Sequencing words 'First,', 'Then,' and 'Finally,' organize steps clearly with commas.

questions.question: Each of the players ___ a water bottle during the match.
options: need
needs
needing
are needing
questions.explanation: 'Each of' takes a singular verb: 'Each of the players needs...'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You don't feel well, do you?
You don't feel well, don't you?
You don't feel well, are you?
You don't feel well, feel you?
questions.explanation: Negative statement + positive tag: 'You don't feel well, do you?'
